name: Dresden
title: Holidays in Dresden
intro: Germany's oldest Christmas market, the home of Stollen cake, in a baroque city rebuilt along the River Elbe. Here's what Dresden is like, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Late November to Christmas Eve is when the Striezelmarkt and a dozen smaller markets are on. May to September is warm, with river boats and beer gardens. January and February are cold and quiet.

things.name: Striezelmarkt
things.blurb: Running since 1434, with a giant wooden Christmas pyramid, a huge walk-through arch and stalls of handmade wooden toys.

things.name: Stollen Festival
things.blurb: On the Saturday before the second Sunday of Advent, a giant Stollen cake is paraded through town and sliced up.

things.name: Frauenkirche
things.blurb: The domed church destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt stone by stone. Climb the dome for the views.

things.name: Zwinger Palace
things.blurb: A baroque palace with galleries of porcelain, paintings and old scientific instruments.

things.name: Paddle steamer
things.blurb: Ride one of the world's oldest fleets of paddle steamers along the Elbe. Most run spring to autumn.

things.name: Saxon Switzerland
things.blurb: Sandstone towers and the Bastei Bridge, under an hour away by train.

faqs.question: Is Dresden good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's good value, the markets have rides and wooden toys, and the old town is easy to walk round.

faqs.question: When is the Striezelmarkt on?
faqs.answer: Usually from late November to 24 December. The Stollen Festival is on one Saturday in early December.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three nights is enough for the markets and museums, or longer with a day in Saxon Switzerland.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper than other German Christmas markets?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Hotels in Dresden tend to cost less than in Cologne or Nuremberg, though flight choices from the UK are fewer.
